subject: SIG: Hosting responsibilities & evidence — Greenleaf follow-up
message_1_body:
Hi Priyom,

We're working through a SIG for Greenleaf and have a handful of hosting-specific questions we need clarified for our info security team. The attached file (greenleaf-sig-baseline.xlsx) highlights the SIG items where we need an explicit mapping to Redwood's operational responsibility. High-level asks: 

- For each hosting mode (Hosted / Dedicated / Private-VPC / On-prem packaged), please indicate custody of keys, responsibility for network egress controls, and where audit logs are retained.
- Which modes support customer-managed KMS/HSM and how does key rotation / revocation work?
- Are there configuration differences that change the shared-responsibility split (e.g., Dedicated in Redwood VPC vs Dedicated in customer VPC)?
- Any standard artifacts you can provide (network diagram, SLA excerpt, SOC2 scope) would help accelerate vendor review.

Can you provide a short mapping table and any supporting artifacts? If easier, we can set a short call — we're targeting completion of our SIG by next Wednesday.

Thanks,
Marta Ruiz
Head of Security Operations
Greenleaf AI

Attachment: greenleaf-sig-baseline.xlsx (sheet: hosting_questions)
message_2_subject: Re: SIG questionnaire: clarifying hosting responsibilities (Greenleaf)
message_2_body:
Hi Marta — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Laura (acct lead) and Aditya (security) so we can provide a short, customer-friendly mapping and attach supporting files.

Quick answers up-front: 
- Hosted: Redwood controls keys and runtime; we provide SOC2-scoped logs and redaction controls. Customer data separation is enforced by tenancy and request-level routing; prefix caching is tenant-isolated.
- Dedicated: Customers get a dedicated GPU pool in our infra. Keys can be Redwood-managed or customer-managed via KMS in certain regions; audit logs are retained per the Dedicated contract (default 90 days, can be extended).
- Private / VPC / On-prem: Customer controls keys, networking, and logging; Redwood's control plane is optional (we can offer offline manifests for on-prem).

We'll produce a short mapping table and attach a single evidence pack (redwood-hosting-evidence-pack.zip) containing an architecture diagram, sample SLA excerpt, and a SIG answer table. Can you do a 30-min sync today at 3pm PT? If not, we can reply in-line.

Best,
Priyom Das
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-hosting-evidence-pack.zip (contains: hosting_matrix.pdf, sla_excerpt.pdf, sig-answer-table.csv)
message_3_subject: Re: SIG questionnaire: clarifying hosting responsibilities (Greenleaf)
message_3_body:
Marta —

Following up with the technical details you flagged. I'm attaching a network diagram and the SIG answer table for the hosting section. Key points by mode: 

1) Hosted (Redwood-managed):
- Encryption in transit: TLS 1.2+/mutual TLS for control plane where applicable.
- Encryption at rest: Managed by Redwood. Keys are Redwood KMS-backed; we provide key footprint details in the evidence pack.
- Audit logs: Aggregated in our logging cluster and retained per tenant policy; default retention 90 days, archived options available.
- Customer responsibility: prompt construction, sensitive PII redaction in prompts, client-side encryption for additional protection.

2) Dedicated (tenant-dedicated compute in Redwood infra):
- Can be Redwood-managed KMS or customer KMS (bring-your-own-key) in supported cloud regions; when customer KMS is used, access controls and rotation are under customer KMS policies.
- Network isolation: dedicated subnets; optional VPC peering (case-by-case) — this is a configuration toggle that affects our ingress/egress model.
- Audit logs: stored in a dedicated project/instance and can be forwarded to customer logging sinks (S3/GCS/CloudWatch) per contract.

3) Private (VPC / on-prem):
- Customer owns KMS/HSM and audit logs; Redwood provides an installer and optional management plane connectors.
- On-prem package supports fully air-gapped deployments where the control plane is absent; we include deployment checklists and runbook excerpts in the evidence pack.

A couple of clarifications for SIG mapping: 
- "Hosted" means Redwood processes requests on shared infrastructure but enforces tenant isolation at the runtime layer (no cross-tenant KV reuse).
- "Dedicated" still runs Redwood runtime; it's dedicated compute but may remain under some Redwood operational controls unless explicitly contracted as customer-owned VPC.
- "Private/on-prem" shifts most operational controls to the customer.

Links and artifacts: 
- Evidence folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b-redwood-hosting-evidence
- Network diagram attached: network-diagram.png
- SIG answer table attached: sig-answer-table.csv

If you need specific legal wording for contract annexes around KMS or log custody, Laura can pull standard clause language.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Security Engineering
Redwood Inference

3) Can you provide the specific SLA excerpt you mentioned and a sample contract clause for KMS responsibility we can drop into our vendor review?

If you can send those as an attachment or a quick redlined clause that would be ideal. We're aiming to close screening by 2027-03-30.

Best,
Marta
